title: The Forgotten Veil
premise: Oscar Galloway was exiled to the Veiled Valley as a child, the only place in the world where her storm-calling magic cannot reach — and where, she believed, she was safe from the court that sold her sister's soul. When the valley's border wards collapse on the night every star goes dark, Oscar is dragged into a dying world where the long winter is a weapon being forged beneath the mountain by the Hollow Court. Guided by a disgraced ward-smith and haunted by fragments of her stolen sister's memories, Oscar must infiltrate the court and steal back the soul before winter seals the world forever. She succeeds only by surrendering her own magic into the veil, restoring the stars at the cost of her power — and discovering that belonging was never something exile could take from her.
about_author: Lior Villalobos is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction about what hides inside them. They write cold, luminous fantasy about exiles, debts, and the families we build in unforgiving places.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Establishes daily life in the Veiled Valley: magicless, quiet, suffocating. Oscar tends the beacon-farm and hides her dormant storm-sense like an old shame. A stranger arrives at the gate asking questions about the wards. Emotional beat: restless unease — safety that feels like a cage.

chapters.title: Wards Like Old Bones
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The valley elder refuses to investigate the weakening border stones; Oscar goes alone at night and finds them scorched from the outside. The stranger, ward-smith Sefa Anwar, catches her there and reveals the wards were sabotaged deliberately. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Dual POV (Oscar/Sefa). Every star vanishes at once; the wards shatter; cold pours over the valley like water. In the chaos, something calls Oscar's name in her sister's voice. Emotional beat: terror and grief colliding as the safe world ends.

chapters.title: What Followed Her Home
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Survivors regroup; Sefa recognizes the sabotage signature of the Hollow Court and confesses he once served them. He tells Oscar the voice she heard means a soul-anchor still exists — hers to find. Emotional beat: guilt offered as alliance, cautiously accepted.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The valley votes to flee south; Oscar chooses instead to follow the soul-thread pulling toward the mountain. First use of her storm-calling beyond the veil — wild, painful, exhilarating. Emotional beat: leaving belonging behind to chase family.

chapters.title: Road of Frozen Bells
chapters.summary: Oscar and Sefa travel through villages already silenced by unnatural frost. They rescue a child, Ilo, whose village sold its warmth to the Court for survival. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh — complicity everywhere, judgment nowhere easy.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ilo's POV. At a tollhouse, passage costs a memory each. Oscar pays one of her sister and doesn't remember paying it; Sefa notices. Emotional beat: quiet horror — survival is a ledger, and someone is keeping it.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Approach to the mountain; Sefa explains the Hollow Court trades in souls and seasons, and that the stolen stars are being forged into an eternal winter crown. First glimpse of the Court's heralds. Emotional beat: scale of the enemy revealed, hope shrinking.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Was Sold
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Flashback interwoven with present: how their mother sold Wren's soul to buy Oscar's exile — protection disguised as abandonment. Oscar realizes she was the payment's shadow, not its beneficiary. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as sacrifice, then reframed again.

chapters.title: Heralds of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Ambush by heralds; Oscar's uncontrolled storms save them but nearly kill Ilo. Sefa demands she learn control or leave. Emotional beat: power as danger to the people she's trying to protect.

chapters.title: Lessons in Thunder
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Training sequence in a frozen gorge; Sefa teaches her that storms obey want, not anger. Oscar touches the soul-thread and hears Wren clearly for the first time: 'Don't come.' Emotional beat: intimacy between allies, and a warning ignored.

chapters.title: The City That Paid Its Warmth
chapters.summary: Ilo's POV. The party shelters in a city that bought a decade of summer by feeding neighbors to the Court. Ilo confronts a cousin who signed the contract. Emotional beat: corruption shown not as monsters but as arithmetic.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A Court agent offers Oscar Wren's freedom in exchange for her storm-magic — the same deal her mother refused. Oscar almost signs. Sefa burns the contract. Emotional beat: temptation crystallized; trust fractured.

chapters.title: What Sefa Buried
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Revelation: Sefa designed the original valley wards — and built the flaw the Court exploited. He came back to undo his work. Oscar must decide whether his penance buys forgiveness. Emotional beat: anger giving way to shared burden.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They enter the mountain through the drowned mine-shafts, guided by Ilo's knowledge of old contracts. The deeper they go, the more of Oscar's paid-away memories surface in the stone. Emotional beat: claustrophobic courage; the past literally surrounding her.

chapters.title: The Soul Vault
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They find the vault: thousands of souls in glass, including Wren's — awake, aware, watching. Guards are souls themselves, hollowed into service. Emotional beat: heartbreak and horror; rescue suddenly feels impossible.

chapters.title: The Winter Crown
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Court unveils the crown mid-forging; without the stars, the long winter becomes permanent within days. Sefa realizes the vault's glass can be turned against the crown — if someone feeds it enough raw power. Emotional beat: plan formed around a terrible cost.

chapters.title: Storm Against Stone
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Climax begins: Oscar unleashes everything to breach the throne hall while Sefa and Ilo reach the vault. The Hollow Queen offers Oscar her sister AND her magic — all she must do is kneel. Emotional beat: fury meeting seduction of power.

chapters.title: The Price of the Veil
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Climax. Oscar refuses, shatters the crown with the last of her storms, and pours her magic through the broken glass to free the souls and relight the stars. Wren's soul returns to a body long dead — but her voice stays long enough to say goodbye. Emotional beat: sacrifice, release, grief and triumph at once.

chapters.title: After the Stars Return
chapters.summary: Ilo's POV. The Court collapses; the freed souls scatter home on the thawing wind. The survivors climb out of the mountain into starlight. Ilo, orphaned twice over, asks Oscar what happens now. Emotional beat: exhausted wonder; the first warm morning.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Unwritten
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar returns to the valley powerless, expecting exile's coldness — and finds the community rebuilding the wards together, Sefa among them, teaching rather than hiding. She is asked to stay not as protector but as neighbor. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Veil Remembers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue. Seasons later, Oscar plants a beacon-stone for Wren at the repaired border. On windless nights she swears she feels weather coming anyway — a ghost of storms in her bones. Emotional beat: quiet peace with an open door; some prices leave gifts behind.
